llm.summary: This is a coherent translation skill that keeps local translation memory and job records, with the main caution being disclosed automatic local record-keeping.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads and writes local Clawic data under translate plus shared contacts, projects, and finances boxes; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but may include sensitive client or business context.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is markdown guidance plus metadata; no executable scripts, package installs, background workers, or auto-install of related skills were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad for translation tasks and the skill applies saved defaults, but it includes clear exclusions for adjacent non-translation work and the behavior is tied to translation quality.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It automatically writes durable local records and may move or delete sections inside its own memory structure without per-write confirmation; this is disclosed, scoped to local memory files, and paired with instructions not to store secrets or full source documents unless requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capabilities match the stated translation/localization purpose: locale choice, glossaries, translation memory, QA, job scoping, and delivery records.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want a translator that maintains local glossaries, style decisions, delivery history, contacts, project pointers, and subscription cost notes under ~/Clawic/data/. Review those local files periodically, and avoid asking it to retain confidential source text or secrets unless you deliberately want a sanitized reference saved.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: The local translation memory and glossary reads are central to consistent returning-client translation work; the artifact also says local storage should avoid secrets and full source documents.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad invocation phrasing covers actual translation/localization cases, while the artifact excludes native copywriting and audio caption generation.
[SQP-3] expected: Locale naming and saved defaults are used to prevent ambiguous translations; this can produce assumptions, but it is a translation-quality behavior rather than unrelated authority.
[SQP-2] expected: Job query logs, scope-change logs, briefs, and delivery rows are durable local records used to manage translation work; users should know they are written automatically.
[SQP-2] expected: The memory template explicitly allows local writes without asking each time; this is disclosed and scoped, but it is the main transparency caveat for installation.
[SQP-2] expected: Consulting client-specific translation memory is expected for this skill, and the artifact contains confidentiality limits that reduce but do not eliminate sensitivity.
[RA2] expected: The split-and-delete procedure is internal memory housekeeping after moving content into indexed files, not deletion of source translation files; it lacks a backup or confirmation step, so users should review that behavior.
